title: Ed Lewis and Red Nichols
summary: Ed Lewis replaced Keyes, and they wonder why he idolized Red Nichols when most players followed Armstrong or Cootie.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: No, Benny had a different set, yes. Set of guys. But he was a good trumpet player. A good high note man. Then we got Ed Lewis in his place.
Now where is Ed from?
Ed's from Kansas.
Oh, he's from Kansas?
Oh, he was with, he was......
He was with Benny. Moten.
Eddie was.
He was a big shot with Benny. Sing and talk.
Oh?
He played like Red Nichols. That was his idol.
Really? That seems funny to me. I can't understand that.
One of the few, one of the few black musicians that tried to play like Red Nichols and he did pretty good at it.
I mean, at best Red Nichols, I mean he had ideas, but he used to sound
like sort of a inferior sort of a Bix Beiderbecke.
Yes, well that's what Ed liked.
Yes, well I mean, what did he like the sort of, I mean, did he like the kind of precision of it or what was it, I mean?
I don't know. I don't know whether it was the style he liked.
That is strange.
Yes, because I don't know anybody else that imitated, everybody was trying to play like Louis or Cootie or.....
Yes, because I remember there were people like Joe Smith and Cootie around.
Joe Smith, yes.
And Louis.
